questions.q: What are two examples of social infrastructure mentioned in the text?
questions.a: Schools and hospitals are two examples of social infrastructure. A wrong answer (like "factories" or "dams") reveals that the student is confusing social infrastructure with physical or economic infrastructure.

questions.q: Why is a school building considered an "investment in the future"?
questions.a: It is an investment because it provides the knowledge and skills that children need to succeed in their adult lives. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks of a school only as a physical structure, missing its role in human development.

questions.q: If a village only has factories but no schools or clinics, why might it struggle in the long term?
questions.a: The village would struggle because the people would lack the health and education needed to work effectively in those factories. A wrong answer indicates the student does not understand that people are the primary drivers of economic activity.

questions.q: Compare a hospital to a road. How are they different in terms of their purpose?
questions.a: A road is physical infrastructure that helps transport goods, while a hospital is social infrastructure that helps maintain the health of the people who produce those goods. A wrong answer shows the student cannot distinguish between supporting economic activity versus supporting human well-being.

questions.q: Should a community prioritize building a new luxury shopping mall or a library if they want to improve social infrastructure?
questions.a: They should prioritize the library because it directly supports education and learning, which are key parts of social infrastructure. A wrong answer shows a misunderstanding of the term "social infrastructure" as anything that is simply "nice to have."

questions.q: Design a small community center. What features would you include to make it a piece of "social infrastructure"?
questions.a: A good answer would include a reading room, a health check-up corner, or space for skill-learning workshops. A poor answer would just list generic things like "a cafe," which serves commerce rather than human development.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Social ______ refers to the essential public facilities, such as schools and hospitals, that support human development and improve the quality of life for a community.
Fill in the blank: Think about your school ______—why do you go there every day?
What is Social infrastructure? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Social infrastructure refers to the essential public facilities, such as schools and hospitals, that support human development and improve the quality of life for a community.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Social infrastructure?
questions.a: Students often think "infrastructure" only means things made of concrete and steel, like roads or bridges.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to categorize a list of community facilities into either physical or social infrastructure and explain why a school is classified as social infrastructure.
